content.en:
LECTURE 32b Stage 5 → Stage 6 Bridge

Your LLM in the Real World: Frontend, API & Custom Training

From Trained Model to Production System: Chat UI, REST API, Custom Data & Commercial Fallbacks
55 min read Intermediate–Advanced Bridge: from “I built it” to “I can ship it”

Why This Lecture Exists

In Lecture 32 you completed the Stage 5 Capstone: a working Mini GPT-2 that generates text. Congratulations — that is a genuine achievement. But a model sitting in a Jupyter notebook is not a product. Nobody outside your terminal can use it. Nobody can send it a question and get an answer back. And it was trained on generic data, not your data.

This bridge lecture closes that gap. We will build a complete, production-ready stack around your Mini GPT-2: a beautiful chat frontend, a REST API that serves the model, a document loader that lets you train on your own files, a guide to finding high-quality training data, and a unified provider interface that lets you fall back to commercial APIs (OpenAI, Gemini, Claude) when you need more power.

By the end, you will have a system you can actually deploy — a real LLM product, not just a model.

What we are building: A full-stack LLM application. Frontend (HTML/CSS/JS) → REST API (FastAPI) → Model backend (your Mini GPT-2 or a commercial API). Plus: a document ingestion pipeline for custom training data and a deployment configuration for Docker and cloud platforms.

Part 1: Build a Chat Frontend for Your LLM

Every LLM product needs a user interface. The most natural interface for a language model is a chat window — a place where users type messages and the model responds. We are going to build one from scratch, using nothing but HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript.

Our chat frontend will include several features that make it feel professional: a dark-themed interface with smooth animations, message bubbles that distinguish between user and assistant messages, a typing indicator that shows when the model is generating, and a settings panel where users can adjust temperature and maximum token count.

The key architectural decision is streaming. When a user sends a message, we do not wait for the entire response to be generated before showing it. Instead, we use the Fetch API with a ReadableStream to display tokens as they arrive. This gives the user immediate feedback and makes the application feel responsive, even when generation takes several seconds.

The frontend communicates with our API server (which we will build in Part 2) via HTTP POST requests to a /generate endpoint. The request body contains the prompt, temperature, and max_tokens parameters. The response streams back token by token using Server-Sent Events (SSE).

One subtle but important detail: we maintain a conversation history on the client side. Each time the user sends a message, we prepend the full conversation history to the prompt. This gives the model context about what has been discussed, even though our Mini GPT-2 does not have a built-in chat memory. The history is stored in a JavaScript array and rendered as message bubbles in the UI.

HTML

Part 2: Expose Your LLM as a REST API

A chat frontend is useless without a backend to power it. We need a server that loads our trained Mini GPT-2 model, accepts HTTP requests, runs inference, and returns generated text. FastAPI is the ideal framework for this: it is fast, supports async operations, generates automatic API documentation, and handles request validation through Pydantic models.

Our API server exposes three endpoints. The POST /generate endpoint accepts a prompt and generation parameters, then returns the generated text. The POST /chat endpoint accepts a list of messages (in the OpenAI-compatible format) and returns an assistant response. The GET /health endpoint returns the server status and model information, useful for monitoring and load balancer health checks.

Security matters even for internal tools. We implement two important protections: CORS configuration to control which domains can call our API, and API key authentication through a custom middleware. The API key is read from an environment variable and checked on every request (except the health endpoint). This prevents unauthorized access and makes it safe to expose the API to the internet.

We also implement streaming responses using FastAPI’s StreamingResponse. Instead of generating the entire response and returning it at once, we yield tokens one at a time. This pairs with the streaming frontend we built in Part 1. The server sends each token as a Server-Sent Event (SSE), and the frontend displays it immediately.

The model is loaded once at startup using FastAPI’s lifespan context manager. This ensures the model weights are in memory before the first request arrives, and properly cleaned up when the server shuts down. Loading a model on every request would be catastrophically slow.

Python

Part 3: Train on Your Own Documents

A language model trained on generic internet text is useful, but a language model trained on your data is powerful. Imagine an LLM that knows your company’s products, your team’s coding conventions, your organization’s policies, or your personal notes. That is what custom training enables.

The first step is document ingestion: reading files from a folder and converting them into clean text that a model can train on. Our DocumentLoader class handles four common formats. Plain text files (.txt) are read directly. Markdown files (.md) are processed to strip formatting syntax (headers, bold, links) while preserving the text content. PDF files are extracted using PyPDF2, which reads each page and concatenates the text. Word documents (.docx) are processed using the python-docx library, extracting text from each paragraph.

The loader scans folders recursively, descending into subdirectories to find all documents. This means you can point it at your entire project folder, your documentation directory, or your notes archive, and it will find and process every supported file.

After loading raw text, we need to clean and chunk it. Cleaning involves normalizing whitespace, removing control characters, and optionally stripping HTML tags or code blocks. Chunking splits long documents into fixed-size pieces (typically 512 or 1024 tokens) with overlap between chunks. The overlap ensures that no information is lost at chunk boundaries — a sentence that spans two chunks will appear in full in at least one of them.

The result is a list of clean text chunks, each suitable as a training example. We can feed these directly into our Mini GPT-2’s training loop, or save them to disk for later use. The code block below includes a complete demonstration: it creates sample files in different formats, loads them, cleans the text, and chunks it into training examples.

Pro Tip: Data quality matters more than data quantity. A small, clean, well-curated dataset will produce better results than a large, noisy one. Always inspect your training data manually before starting a training run. Remove duplicates, fix encoding issues, and ensure the text is representative of what you want the model to learn.
Python

Part 4: Where to Find Training Data

Building a great language model requires great data. But where do you find it? The landscape of training data sources is vast, and choosing the right ones depends on your use case, your computational budget, and your legal obligations.

Public large-scale datasets are the foundation of most LLM training. Common Crawl is the largest: a regularly updated archive of billions of web pages. The Pile (by EleutherAI) is a curated 800GB dataset combining 22 diverse sources including books, academic papers, code, and web text. RedPajama is an open reproduction of the LLaMA training dataset. C4 (Colossal Clean Crawled Corpus) is a cleaned version of Common Crawl used to train T5. These datasets are freely available but require significant storage and processing.

The HuggingFace Datasets library is the easiest way to access training data. With a single line of code — load_dataset("wikitext", "wikitext-103-v1") — you can download and start using high-quality text data. The library handles downloading, caching, and preprocessing. It supports hundreds of datasets across dozens of languages and domains.

Domain-specific sources are crucial when you want your model to excel in a particular area. For scientific text, arXiv provides millions of research papers. For general knowledge, Wikipedia dumps are freely available in over 300 languages. For literature, Project Gutenberg offers over 70,000 public domain books. For code, GitHub repositories (with appropriate licenses) and The Stack dataset provide billions of lines of source code.

Your own data is often the most valuable. Internal documents, emails (with proper consent), technical manuals, customer support transcripts, product documentation, meeting notes — these contain the specific knowledge that makes your model uniquely useful. The DocumentLoader from Part 3 is your tool for ingesting this data.

Finally, data quality guidelines are essential. Deduplicate your data: repeated text teaches the model to be repetitive. Filter for quality: remove very short documents, documents with too many special characters, and auto-generated spam. Check for legal compliance: respect copyright, avoid personally identifiable information (PII), and honor license terms. When in doubt, consult a lawyer before training on data you did not create.

Legal Warning: Training on copyrighted material without permission may violate copyright law in your jurisdiction. Always check the license of any dataset you use. Remove PII (names, emails, phone numbers, addresses) from training data. When using commercial datasets, read the terms of service carefully — some prohibit use in model training.
Python

Part 5: Connect Your LLM to Commercial APIs (Fallback)

Your Mini GPT-2 is an impressive achievement, but let us be honest: it has limitations. With its small parameter count and limited training data, it cannot match the quality of commercial models like GPT-4, Gemini, or Claude for complex tasks. The pragmatic solution is a hybrid approach: use your own model when speed, privacy, or cost matter, and fall back to commercial APIs when you need higher quality.

There are compelling reasons to keep your own model in the loop. Privacy: sensitive data never leaves your servers. Speed: a small local model responds in milliseconds, while API calls take seconds. Cost: after the initial training investment, inference is free. Availability: your model works offline and is not affected by API outages or rate limits. But for tasks that require deep reasoning, broad knowledge, or nuanced language understanding, commercial models are currently superior.

Our UnifiedLLMProvider class creates a clean abstraction over multiple backends. It exposes a single generate() method that works identically regardless of whether the backend is your own model, OpenAI, Google Gemini, or Anthropic Claude. A single configuration variable — provider — controls which backend is used. Switching from your own model to Claude is a one-line config change.

Each commercial API has its own authentication mechanism, request format, and response structure. Our provider class handles all of these differences internally. For OpenAI, we use the openai library and the chat completions endpoint. For Gemini, we use the google-generativeai library. For Claude, we use the anthropic library with the messages API. The code includes proper error handling, retry logic, and timeout configuration.

The demo below runs entirely in your browser using mock responses (since we cannot make real API calls from Pyodide). But the provider interface is production-ready — replace the mock functions with real API calls and it works immediately.

Python

Part 6: Putting It All Together

Now we have all the pieces: a chat frontend, a REST API, a document loader, training data sources, and a unified provider interface. The final step is to combine them into a deployable system.

The architecture is clean and modular:


┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    USER'S BROWSER                       │
│  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │           Chat Frontend (index.html)              │  │
│  │   HTML/CSS/JS • Dark Theme • Streaming Display    │  │
│  └──────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘  │
└─────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┘
                          │ HTTP POST /generate
                          │ (SSE streaming)
┌─────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┐
│              FastAPI Server (main.py)                    │
│  ┌──────────────────────┴────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │   /generate  •  /chat  •  /health                 │  │
│  │   CORS  •  API Key Auth  •  Rate Limiting          │  │
│  └──────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘  │
│                         │                                │
│  ┌──────────────────────┴────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │         UnifiedLLMProvider                        │  │
│  │  ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌─────────┐ ┌──────┐  │  │
│  │  │ Own GPT-2│ │ OpenAI   │ │ Gemini  │ │Claude│  │  │
│  │  └──────────┘ └──────────┘ └─────────┘ └──────┘  │  │
│  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Docker Compose bundles everything into containers. The frontend is served by Nginx, the API runs in a Python container with uvicorn, and the model files are stored in a shared volume. A single docker compose up brings the entire stack online.

For cloud deployment, platforms like Railway and Render make it easy to go from a Git repository to a live URL. Both support Docker-based deployments, automatic HTTPS, environment variable management, and horizontal scaling. The deployment script below automates the process with step-by-step instructions.

Before deploying, review this environment variables checklist:

  • API_KEY — Your API authentication key (generate a random string)
  • MODEL_PATH — Path to your trained model weights
  • DEFAULT_PROVIDER — Which LLM backend to use: own, openai, gemini, or claude
  • OPENAI_API_KEY — Required if using OpenAI as fallback
  • GOOGLE_API_KEY — Required if using Gemini as fallback
  • ANTHROPIC_API_KEY — Required if using Claude as fallback
  • MAX_TOKENS — Default maximum tokens per generation (e.g., 256)
  • CORS_ORIGINS — Comma-separated list of allowed frontend URLs
YAML
Bash

What Comes Next

You now have a complete, deployable LLM system. But this is just the beginning. In Stage 6, we will explore fine-tuning — the art of taking a pre-trained model and specializing it for a specific task. Fine-tuning is how you turn a general-purpose language model into a domain expert: a medical assistant, a legal analyzer, a code generator, or anything else you can imagine.

The infrastructure you built in this lecture — the API server, the document loader, the provider interface — will serve as the foundation for everything that follows. You are no longer just building models. You are building products.

Key Takeaway: A model without infrastructure is a science project. A model with a frontend, an API, custom training data, and a deployment pipeline is a product. You now have both.

LECTURE 32b Etapa 5 → Etapa 6 Punte

Lecția 32b: LLM-ul Tãu în Lumea Realã: Frontend, API și Antrenament Personalizat

De la Model Antrenat la Sistem de Producție: UI de Chat, API REST, Date Proprii și Fallback-uri Comerciale
55 min lecturã Intermediar–Avansat Punte: de la „l-am construit” la „îl pot livra”

De ce existã aceastã lecție

În Lecția 32 ai finalizat Capstone-ul Etapei 5: un Mini GPT-2 funcțional care genereazã text. Felicitãri — aceasta este o realizare autentică. Dar un model care stã într-un notebook Jupyter nu este un produs. Nimeni din afara terminalului tãu nu îl poate folosi.

Aceastã lecție-punte închide acest decalaj. Vom construi un stack complet în jurul Mini GPT-2: un frontend de chat, un API REST, un încãrcãtor de documente pentru antrenament pe datele tale, un ghid pentru gãsirea datelor de antrenament și o interfață unificatã de provider care permite fallback cãtre API-uri comerciale.

Ce construim: O aplicație LLM full-stack. Frontend (HTML/CSS/JS) → API REST (FastAPI) → Backend model (Mini GPT-2 sau API comercial). Plus: pipeline de ingestie documente și configurație de deployment.

Partea 1: Construiește un Frontend de Chat

Fiecare produs LLM are nevoie de o interfață. Interfața cea mai naturalã pentru un model de limbaj este o fereastrã de chat. Vom construi una de la zero, folosind HTML, CSS și JavaScript vanilla.

Frontend-ul include: temã întunecatã cu animații, bule de mesaje pentru utilizator și asistent, indicator de tastare în timpul generării, și un panou de setări pentru temperatură și număr maxim de token-uri.

Decizia arhitecturală cheie este streaming-ul. Când utilizatorul trimite un mesaj, nu așteptãm rãspunsul complet. Folosim Fetch API cu ReadableStream pentru a afișa token-urile pe mãsurã ce sosesc.

HTML

Partea 2: Expune LLM-ul ca API REST

Un frontend de chat este inutil fãrã un backend. Avem nevoie de un server care încarcã modelul Mini GPT-2, acceptã cereri HTTP, ruleazã inferența și returneazã textul generat. FastAPI este framework-ul ideal.

Serverul expune trei endpoint-uri: POST /generate pentru generare de text, POST /chat pentru conversații în format compatibil OpenAI, și GET /health pentru monitorizare. Implementãm CORS și autentificare prin cheie API.

Modelul se încarcã o singurã datã la pornire folosind context manager-ul lifespan al FastAPI. Streaming-ul se face prin StreamingResponse și Server-Sent Events.

Python

Partea 3: Antrenare pe Documentele Tale

Un model antrenat pe text generic de pe internet este util, dar un model antrenat pe datele tale este puternic. Clasa DocumentLoader gestioneazã patru formate: .txt (citire directã), .md (eliminare sintaxã markdown), .pdf (extracție cu PyPDF2) și .docx (procesare cu python-docx).

Loader-ul scaneazã foldere recursiv. Dupã încãrcarea textului brut, îl curãță și îl împarte în chunk-uri de dimensiune fixã cu suprapunere.

Sfat Pro: Calitatea datelor conteazã mai mult decât cantitatea. Un dataset mic și curat va produce rezultate mai bune decât unul mare și zgomotos.
Python

Partea 4: Unde Gãsești Date de Antrenament

Dataset-uri publice: Common Crawl, The Pile, RedPajama, C4. HuggingFace Datasets: acces ușor cu load_dataset(). Surse specifice: arXiv, Wikipedia, Project Gutenberg. Datele tale: documente interne, emailuri, manuale.

Linii directoare de calitate: deduplicare, filtrare, verificare lungime. Aspecte legale: copyright, PII, licențiere.

Avertisment Legal: Antrenarea pe material protejat de copyright fãrã permisiune poate încãlca legea. Verifică întotdeauna licența. Eliminã PII din datele de antrenament.
Python

Partea 5: Conectare la API-uri Comerciale (Fallback)

Mini GPT-2 are limitări. Soluția pragmatică este o abordare hibridă: modelul propriu pentru viteză/confidențialitate, API-uri comerciale pentru calitate. Clasa UnifiedLLMProvider creează o abstracție curată peste multiple backend-uri.

Motivele pentru modelul propriu: Confidențialitate (datele nu pãrãsesc serverele tale), Viteză (milisecunde vs secunde), Cost (inferența gratuitã), Disponibilitate (funcționeazã offline).

Python

Partea 6: Totul Laolaltã

Arhitectura: Frontend → API FastAPI → UnifiedLLMProvider → Model (propriu sau comercial). Docker Compose împachetează totul în containere. Platforme ca Railway și Render fac deployment-ul simplu.

Variabile de mediu necesare: API_KEY, MODEL_PATH, DEFAULT_PROVIDER, chei API pentru provideri comerciali, MAX_TOKENS, CORS_ORIGINS.

YAML
Bash

Ce Urmează

Acum ai un sistem LLM complet, gata de deployment. În Etapa 6, vom explora fine-tuning-ul — arta de a lua un model pre-antrenat și de a-l specializa pentru o sarcinã specifică.

Concluzie Cheie: Un model fãrã infrastructură este un proiect științific. Un model cu frontend, API, date de antrenament proprii și pipeline de deployment este un produs. Acum le ai pe amândouã.
content.el:
LECTURE 32b Στάδιο 5 → Στάδιο 6 Γέφυρα

Διάλεξη 32b: Το LLM σου στον Πραγματικό Κόσμο: Frontend, API & Προσαρμοσμένη Εκπαίδευση

Από Εκπαιδευμένο Μοντέλο σε Σύστημα Παραγωγής: Chat UI, REST API, Προσαρμοσμένα Δεδομένα & Εμπορικά Fallbacks
55 λεπτά ανάγνωση Μεσαίο–Προχωρημένο Γέφυρα: από «το έφτιαξα» σε «μπορώ να το στείλω»

Γιατί Υπάρχει αυτή η Διάλεξη

Στη Διάλεξη 32 ολοκληρώσατε το Capstone του Σταδίου 5: ένα λειτουργικό Mini GPT-2 που παράγει κείμενο. Συγχαρητήρια — αυτό είναι ένα πραγματικό επίτευγμα. Αλλά ένα μοντέλο σε ένα Jupyter notebook δεν είναι προϊόν. Κανείς εκτός του τερματικού σας δεν μπορεί να το χρησιμοποιήσει.

Αυτή η γεφυρική διάλεξη κλείνει αυτό το κενό. Θα χτίσουμε ένα πλήρες stack γύρω από το Mini GPT-2: frontend chat, REST API, φορτωτή εγγράφων για εκπαίδευση στα δικά σας δεδομένα, οδηγό για εύρεση δεδομένων εκπαίδευσης και ενοποιημένη διεπαφή provider.

Τι χτίζουμε: Μια full-stack εφαρμογή LLM. Frontend (HTML/CSS/JS) → REST API (FastAPI) → Backend μοντέλου (Mini GPT-2 ή εμπορικό API). Επιπλέον: pipeline εισαγωγής εγγράφων και ρύθμιση deployment.

Μέρος 1: Κατασκευή Frontend Chat

Κάθε προϊόν LLM χρειάζεται διεπαφή χρήστη. Η πιο φυσική διεπαφή για ένα γλωσσικό μοντέλο είναι ένα παράθυρο chat. Θα φτιάξουμε ένα από το μηδέν με HTML, CSS και vanilla JavaScript.

Το frontend περιλαμβάνει: σκούρο θέμα με animations, φυσαλίδες μηνυμάτων, δείκτη πληκτρολόγησης κατά τη δημιουργία, και πίνακα ρυθμίσεων για θερμοκρασία και μέγιστο αριθμό tokens. Η βασική αρχιτεκτονική απόφαση είναι το streaming.

HTML

Μέρος 2: Εκθέστε το LLM ως REST API

Χρειαζόμαστε έναν server που φορτώνει το Mini GPT-2, δέχεται HTTP αιτήματα και επιστρέφει κείμενο. Το FastAPI είναι το ιδανικό framework. Τρία endpoints: POST /generate, POST /chat, GET /health.

Υλοποιούμε CORS, αυθεντικοποίηση API key, και streaming responses με Server-Sent Events. Το μοντέλο φορτώνεται μία φορά κατά την εκκίνηση.

Python

Μέρος 3: Εκπαίδευση στα Δικά σας Έγγραφα

Η κλάση DocumentLoader διαχειρίζεται τέσσερις μορφές: .txt, .md, .pdf και .docx. Σαρώνει φακέλους αναδρομικά, καθαρίζει το κείμενο και το χωρίζει σε chunks σταθερού μεγέθους.

Συμβουλή: Η ποιότητα δεδομένων μετράει περισσότερο από την ποσότητα.
Python

Μέρος 4: Πού να Βρείτε Δεδομένα Εκπαίδευσης

Δημόσια datasets: Common Crawl, The Pile, RedPajama, C4. HuggingFace Datasets: εύκολη πρόσβαση με load_dataset(). Ειδικές πηγές: arXiv, Wikipedia, Project Gutenberg. Δικά σας δεδομένα: εσωτερικά έγγραφα, emails, εγχειρίδια.

Νομική Προειδοποίηση: Η εκπαίδευση σε υλικό με πνευματικά δικαιώματα χωρίς άδεια μπορεί να παραβιάζει τον νόμο. Ελέγξτε πάντα την άδεια. Αφαιρέστε PII από τα δεδομένα εκπαίδευσης.
Python

Μέρος 5: Σύνδεση με Εμπορικά APIs (Fallback)

Η πρακτική λύση είναι μια υβριδική προσέγγιση: δικό σας μοντέλο για ταχύτητα/ιδιωτικότητα, εμπορικά APIs για ποιότητα. Η κλάση UnifiedLLMProvider δημιουργεί μια καθαρή αφαίρεση πάνω σε πολλαπλά backends.

Python

Μέρος 6: Όλα Μαζί

Αρχιτεκτονική: Frontend → FastAPI → UnifiedLLMProvider → Μοντέλο. Docker Compose πακετάρει τα πάντα. Πλατφόρμες όπως Railway και Render κάνουν το deployment εύκολο.

YAML
Bash

Τι Ακολουθεί

Τώρα έχετε ένα πλήρες σύστημα LLM. Στο Στάδιο 6, θα εξερευνήσουμε το fine-tuning — την τέχνη της εξειδίκευσης ενός προ-εκπαιδευμένου μοντέλου.

Βασικό Συμπέρασμα: Ένα μοντέλο χωρίς υποδομή είναι ένα επιστημονικό έργο. Ένα μοντέλο με frontend, API, δεδομένα εκπαίδευσης και pipeline deployment είναι ένα προϊόν. Τώρα έχετε και τα δύο.

codeBlocks.title: FastAPI Server for Mini GPT-2
codeBlocks.code:
"""
FastAPI Server for Mini GPT-2
=============================
Run with: uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
"""

import os
import json
import time
import numpy as np
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Optional

from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Request, Depends
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


# ----- Pydantic Models -----

class GenerateRequest(BaseModel):
    prompt: str = Field(..., min_length=1, max_length=4096)
    temperature: float = Field(default=0.7, ge=0.0, le=2.0)
    max_tokens: int = Field(default=128, ge=1, le=1024)
    stream: bool = Field(default=False)

class ChatMessage(BaseModel):
    role: str = Field(..., pattern="^(user|assistant|system)$")
    content: str

class ChatRequest(BaseModel):
    messages: list[ChatMessage]
    temperature: float = Field(default=0.7, ge=0.0, le=2.0)
    max_tokens: int = Field(default=128, ge=1, le=1024)
    stream: bool = Field(default=False)

class GenerateResponse(BaseModel):
    text: str
    tokens_generated: int
    generation_time_ms: float

class HealthResponse(BaseModel):
    status: str
    model_loaded: bool
    model_name: str
    uptime_seconds: float


# ----- Model Loading -----

model_state = {"model": None, "start_time": None}

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    """Load model on startup, clean up on shutdown."""
    print("Loading Mini GPT-2 model...")
    model_path = os.getenv("MODEL_PATH", "./model_weights.npz")

    # In production, load your actual model weights here:
    # model_state["model"] = load_mini_gpt2(model_path)

    # For demonstration, we use a placeholder:
    model_state["model"] = {"loaded": True, "path": model_path}
    model_state["start_time"] = time.time()
    print(f"Model loaded from {model_path}")
    yield
    print("Shutting down, releasing model resources...")
    model_state["model"] = None


# ----- API Key Authentication -----

API_KEY = os.getenv("API_KEY", "dev-key-change-in-production")

async def verify_api_key(request: Request):
    """Middleware to check API key on protected routes."""
    api_key = request.headers.get("X-API-Key")
    if api_key != API_KEY:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Invalid or missing API key")


# ----- FastAPI App -----

app = FastAPI(
    title="Mini GPT-2 API",
    description="REST API for your custom Mini GPT-2 language model",
    version="1.0.0",
    lifespan=lifespan
)

# CORS Configuration
cors_origins = os.getenv("CORS_ORIGINS", "http://localhost:3000").split(",")
app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=cors_origins,
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=["*"],
    allow_headers=["*"],
)


# ----- Helper: Generate Text -----

def generate_text(prompt: str, temperature: float, max_tokens: int):
    """
    Generate text using the loaded model.
    Replace this with your actual Mini GPT-2 inference code.
    """
    # Placeholder: In production, this calls your model's forward pass
    # and sampling loop from Lecture 32.
    words = ["The", "model", "generates", "text", "based", "on",
             "the", "input", "prompt.", "This", "is", "a",
             "placeholder", "response."]
    tokens = []
    for i in range(min(max_tokens, 50)):
        tokens.append(words[i % len(words)])
    return " ".join(tokens)

def generate_text_streaming(prompt: str, temperature: float, max_tokens: int):
    """
    Generator that yields tokens one at a time for streaming.
    """
    words = ["The", "model", "generates", "text", "token",
             "by", "token", "for", "streaming."]
    for i in range(min(max_tokens, 50)):
        token = words[i % len(words)]
        yield token + " "
        time.sleep(0.05)  # Simulate generation time


# ----- Endpoints -----

@app.get("/health", response_model=HealthResponse)
async def health_check():
    """Health check endpoint (no auth required)."""
    return HealthResponse(
        status="healthy",
        model_loaded=model_state["model"] is not None,
        model_name="Mini GPT-2",
        uptime_seconds=time.time() - (model_state["start_time"] or time.time())
    )

@app.post("/generate", response_model=GenerateResponse,
          dependencies=[Depends(verify_api_key)])
async def generate(request: GenerateRequest):
    """Generate text from a prompt."""
    if model_state["model"] is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=503, detail="Model not loaded")

    if request.stream:
        async def event_stream():
            for token in generate_text_streaming(
                request.prompt, request.temperature, request.max_tokens
            ):
                yield f"data: {json.dumps({'token': token})}\n\n"
            yield "data: {\"done\": true}\n\n"

        return StreamingResponse(
            event_stream(),
            media_type="text/event-stream",
            headers={"Cache-Control": "no-cache", "Connection": "keep-alive"}
        )

    start = time.time()
    text = generate_text(request.prompt, request.temperature, request.max_tokens)
    elapsed = (time.time() - start) * 1000

    return GenerateResponse(
        text=text,
        tokens_generated=len(text.split()),
        generation_time_ms=round(elapsed, 2)
    )

@app.post("/chat", dependencies=[Depends(verify_api_key)])
async def chat(request: ChatRequest):
    """Chat endpoint (OpenAI-compatible message format)."""
    if model_state["model"] is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=503, detail="Model not loaded")

    # Build prompt from messages
    prompt = ""
    for msg in request.messages:
        prefix = {"system": "System", "user": "User", "assistant": "Assistant"}
        prompt += f"{prefix[msg.role]}: {msg.content}\n"
    prompt += "Assistant:"

    if request.stream:
        async def event_stream():
            for token in generate_text_streaming(
                prompt, request.temperature, request.max_tokens
            ):
                yield f"data: {json.dumps({'token': token})}\n\n"
            yield "data: {\"done\": true}\n\n"
        return StreamingResponse(event_stream(), media_type="text/event-stream")

    text = generate_text(prompt, request.temperature, request.max_tokens)
    return {
        "role": "assistant",
        "content": text,
        "model": "mini-gpt2",
        "usage": {"prompt_tokens": len(prompt.split()),
                  "completion_tokens": len(text.split())}
    }


# ----- Run -----

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import uvicorn
    uvicorn.run(app, host="0.0.0.0", port=8000)

"""
Document Loader - Train on Your Own Files
==========================================
Loads .txt, .md, .pdf, .docx from a folder, cleans text, and chunks it.
This demo creates sample files and processes them (runs in Pyodide).
"""

import os
import re
import textwrap


class DocumentLoader:
    """Load documents from a folder, supporting multiple formats."""

    SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS = {'.txt', '.md', '.pdf', '.docx'}

    def __init__(self, chunk_size=512, chunk_overlap=64):
        self.chunk_size = chunk_size      # characters per chunk
        self.chunk_overlap = chunk_overlap
        self.documents = []
        self.stats = {'files_found': 0, 'files_loaded': 0,
                      'files_skipped': 0, 'total_chars': 0}

    # --- Format-specific loaders ---

    def load_txt(self, filepath):
        """Load plain text file."""
        with open(filepath, 'r', encoding='utf-8', errors='replace') as f:
            return f.read()

    def load_md(self, filepath):
        """Load markdown file, stripping syntax."""
        with open(filepath, 'r', encoding='utf-8', errors='replace') as f:
            text = f.read()
        # Remove markdown syntax
        text = re.sub(r'^#{1,6}\s+', '', text, flags=re.MULTILINE)  # headers
        text = re.sub(r'\*\*(.+?)\*\*', r'\1', text)    # bold
        text = re.sub(r'\*(.+?)\*', r'\1', text)         # italic
        text = re.sub(r'`{3}[\s\S]*?`{3}', '', text)     # code blocks
        text = re.sub(r'`(.+?)`', r'\1', text)            # inline code
        text = re.sub(r'\[(.+?)\]\(.+?\)', r'\1', text)   # links
        text = re.sub(r'^\s*[-*+]\s+', '', text, flags=re.MULTILINE)  # lists
        text = re.sub(r'^\s*\d+\.\s+', '', text, flags=re.MULTILINE)  # numbered lists
        text = re.sub(r'^>\s+', '', text, flags=re.MULTILINE)  # blockquotes
        text = re.sub(r'---+', '', text)                  # horizontal rules
        return text

    def load_pdf(self, filepath):
        """Load PDF (requires PyPDF2 - shown as example)."""
        # In production:
        # from PyPDF2 import PdfReader
        # reader = PdfReader(filepath)
        # return "\n".join(page.extract_text() for page in reader.pages)
        return f"[PDF content from {os.path.basename(filepath)}]"

    def load_docx(self, filepath):
        """Load Word document (requires python-docx - shown as example)."""
        # In production:
        # from docx import Document
        # doc = Document(filepath)
        # return "\n".join(para.text for para in doc.paragraphs)
        return f"[DOCX content from {os.path.basename(filepath)}]"

    # --- Core methods ---

    def load_file(self, filepath):
        """Load a single file based on its extension."""
        ext = os.path.splitext(filepath)[1].lower()
        loaders = {
            '.txt': self.load_txt,
            '.md': self.load_md,
            '.pdf': self.load_pdf,
            '.docx': self.load_docx,
        }
        if ext not in loaders:
            return None
        try:
            return loaders[ext](filepath)
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"  Warning: Could not load {filepath}: {e}")
            return None

    def scan_folder(self, folder_path, recursive=True):
        """Scan a folder for supported documents."""
        files_found = []
        if recursive:
            for root, dirs, files in os.walk(folder_path):
                for fname in sorted(files):
                    ext = os.path.splitext(fname)[1].lower()
                    if ext in self.SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS:
                        files_found.append(os.path.join(root, fname))
        else:
            for fname in sorted(os.listdir(folder_path)):
                ext = os.path.splitext(fname)[1].lower()
                if ext in self.SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS:
                    files_found.append(os.path.join(folder_path, fname))
        return files_found

    def clean_text(self, text):
        """Clean raw text for training."""
        text = text.replace('\r\n', '\n').replace('\r', '\n')
        text = re.sub(r'[\x00-\x08\x0b\x0c\x0e-\x1f\x7f]', '', text)  # control chars
        text = re.sub(r'\n{3,}', '\n\n', text)  # excessive newlines
        text = re.sub(r' {2,}', ' ', text)       # excessive spaces
        return text.strip()

    def chunk_text(self, text, source=""):
        """Split text into overlapping chunks."""
        chunks = []
        start = 0
        while start < len(text):
            end = start + self.chunk_size
            chunk = text[start:end]
            if chunk.strip():
                chunks.append({
                    'text': chunk,
                    'source': source,
                    'chunk_index': len(chunks),
                    'char_start': start,
                    'char_end': min(end, len(text))
                })
            start += self.chunk_size - self.chunk_overlap
        return chunks

    def load_folder(self, folder_path, recursive=True):
        """Load all documents from a folder, clean, and chunk them."""
        files = self.scan_folder(folder_path, recursive)
        self.stats['files_found'] = len(files)

        all_chunks = []
        for filepath in files:
            text = self.load_file(filepath)
            if text is None:
                self.stats['files_skipped'] += 1
                continue

            text = self.clean_text(text)
            if len(text) < 10:
                self.stats['files_skipped'] += 1
                continue

            chunks = self.chunk_text(text, source=filepath)
            all_chunks.extend(chunks)
            self.stats['files_loaded'] += 1
            self.stats['total_chars'] += len(text)

        self.documents = all_chunks
        return all_chunks


# ============================================================
# DEMO: Create sample files and load them
# ============================================================

print("=" * 60)
print("DOCUMENT LOADER DEMO")
print("=" * 60)

# Create a demo folder with sample files
os.makedirs("/tmp/training_docs/subfolder", exist_ok=True)

# Sample .txt file
with open("/tmp/training_docs/company_overview.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write(textwrap.dedent("""
    Our Company Overview

    We are a technology company specializing in artificial intelligence
    and machine learning solutions. Founded in 2020, we have grown to
    serve over 500 enterprise customers across 30 countries.

    Our flagship product is an AI-powered document analysis platform
    that can process contracts, invoices, and reports automatically.
    The platform uses custom-trained language models to extract key
    information, classify documents, and generate summaries.

    Our engineering team follows agile methodology with two-week sprints.
    We deploy to production multiple times per day using a CI/CD pipeline
    built on GitHub Actions and Kubernetes. All services are containerized
    and orchestrated with Helm charts.
    """).strip())

# Sample .md file
with open("/tmp/training_docs/api_guide.md", "w") as f:
    f.write(textwrap.dedent("""
    # API Guide

    ## Authentication

    All API requests require a **Bearer token** in the `Authorization` header.
    Tokens are obtained via the `/auth/token` endpoint.

    ## Endpoints

    ### POST /analyze

    Analyze a document and return extracted entities.

    ```json
    {
      "document_url": "https://example.com/doc.pdf",
      "analysis_type": "full"
    }
    ```

    ### GET /results/{job_id}

    Retrieve analysis results for a completed job.

    > Note: Results are cached for 24 hours after completion.

    ## Rate Limits

    - Free tier: 100 requests/day
    - Pro tier: 10,000 requests/day
    - Enterprise: *unlimited*
    """).strip())

# Sample file in subfolder
with open("/tmp/training_docs/subfolder/meeting_notes.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write(textwrap.dedent("""
    Team Meeting Notes - Q4 Planning

    Attendees: Alice, Bob, Charlie, Diana

    Key Decisions:
    1. Migrate from PostgreSQL to CockroachDB for multi-region support
    2. Launch the new embedding model by November 15th
    3. Hire two more ML engineers for the fine-tuning team

    Action Items:
    - Alice: Draft migration plan by Friday
    - Bob: Benchmark CockroachDB performance
    - Charlie: Post ML engineer job listings
    - Diana: Prepare Q3 metrics presentation for board
    """).strip())

# Load all documents
loader = DocumentLoader(chunk_size=256, chunk_overlap=32)
chunks = loader.load_folder("/tmp/training_docs", recursive=True)

print(f"\nStatistics:")
print(f"  Files found:   {loader.stats['files_found']}")
print(f"  Files loaded:  {loader.stats['files_loaded']}")
print(f"  Files skipped: {loader.stats['files_skipped']}")
print(f"  Total chars:   {loader.stats['total_chars']:,}")
print(f"  Total chunks:  {len(chunks)}")

print(f"\n{'=' * 60}")
print("SAMPLE CHUNKS")
print(f"{'=' * 60}")

for i, chunk in enumerate(chunks[:4]):
    source = os.path.basename(chunk['source'])
    print(f"\n--- Chunk {i} (from {source}) ---")
    preview = chunk['text'][:120].replace('\n', ' ')
    print(f"  {preview}...")
    print(f"  Length: {len(chunk['text'])} chars, "
          f"Position: {chunk['char_start']}-{chunk['char_end']}")

print(f"\nDone! {len(chunks)} chunks ready for training.")

"""
Training Data Sources & HuggingFace Datasets
=============================================
Demonstrates data source patterns and preprocessing.
(Uses inline data since HuggingFace datasets library is not available in Pyodide)
"""

import re
from collections import Counter


# ============================================================
# Part 1: Simulated HuggingFace Datasets Interface
# ============================================================

class SimulatedDataset:
    """
    Mimics the HuggingFace datasets interface.
    In production, you would use:
        from datasets import load_dataset
        dataset = load_dataset("wikitext", "wikitext-103-v1")
    """

    def __init__(self, name, data):
        self.name = name
        self.data = data
        self.num_rows = len(data)

    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        if isinstance(idx, slice):
            return {'text': self.data[idx]}
        return {'text': self.data[idx]}

    def __len__(self):
        return self.num_rows

    def filter(self, fn):
        filtered = [item for item in self.data if fn({'text': item})]
        return SimulatedDataset(self.name + " (filtered)", filtered)

    def map(self, fn):
        mapped = [fn({'text': item})['text'] for item in self.data]
        return SimulatedDataset(self.name + " (mapped)", mapped)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"Dataset({self.name}, num_rows={self.num_rows})"


def load_dataset(name, split="train"):
    """Simulated load_dataset function."""
    datasets = {
        "wikitext": [
            " = Valkyria Chronicles III = ",
            "",
            " Senjō no Valkyria 3 : Unrecorded Chronicles is a tactical role-playing"
            " video game developed by Sega and Media.Vision for the PlayStation Portable.",
            " Released in January 2011 in Japan, it is the third game in the Valkyria"
            " Chronicles series.",
            "",
            " = Tower Building of the Little Rock Arsenal = ",
            "",
            " The Tower Building of the Little Rock Arsenal, also known as U.S. Arsenal"
            " Building, is a building located in MacArthur Park in downtown Little Rock,"
            " Arkansas.",
            " Built in 1840, it was part of the Little Rock Arsenal, a military"
            " installation built to protect settlers.",
            "",
            " =935th Air Refueling Squadron = ",
            "",
            " The 935th Air Refueling Squadron is an inactive United States Air Force"
            " unit. It was last assigned to the 917th Air Refueling Group.",
            " The squadron was first activated in 1963 as the 935th Air Refueling"
            " Squadron, Heavy, at Biggs Air Force Base, Texas.",
        ],
        "tiny_shakespeare": [
            "ROMEO: But, soft! what light through yonder window breaks?",
            "It is the east, and Juliet is the sun.",
            "Arise, fair sun, and kill the envious moon,",
            "Who is already sick and pale with grief,",
            "That thou her maid art far more fair than she.",
            "",
            "JULIET: O Romeo, Romeo! wherefore art thou Romeo?",
            "Deny thy father and refuse thy name;",
            "Or, if thou wilt not, be but sworn my love,",
            "And I'll no longer be a Capulet.",
        ]
    }
    data = datasets.get(name, ["No data found for this dataset."])
    print(f"  load_dataset('{name}', split='{split}')")
    return SimulatedDataset(name, data)


# ============================================================
# Part 2: Data Quality Pipeline
# ============================================================

class DataQualityPipeline:
    """Process and filter training data for quality."""

    def __init__(self, min_length=20, max_length=10000):
        self.min_length = min_length
        self.max_length = max_length
        self.stats = Counter()

    def is_quality(self, text):
        """Check if a text sample meets quality standards."""
        if not text or not text.strip():
            self.stats['empty'] += 1
            return False

        text = text.strip()

        if len(text) < self.min_length:
            self.stats['too_short'] += 1
            return False

        if len(text) > self.max_length:
            self.stats['too_long'] += 1
            return False

        # Check for excessive special characters
        alpha_ratio = sum(c.isalpha() for c in text) / max(len(text), 1)
        if alpha_ratio < 0.5:
            self.stats['low_alpha'] += 1
            return False

        # Check for repetition (same word repeated many times)
        words = text.lower().split()
        if words:
            most_common_word, count = Counter(words).most_common(1)[0]
            if count / len(words) > 0.3 and len(words) > 10:
                self.stats['repetitive'] += 1
                return False

        self.stats['passed'] += 1
        return True

    def clean(self, text):
        """Clean a text sample."""
        text = text.strip()
        text = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', text)               # normalize whitespace
        text = re.sub(r'http\S+', '[URL]', text)        # replace URLs
        text = re.sub(r'\S+@\S+', '[EMAIL]', text)      # replace emails
        text = re.sub(r'\b\d{3}[-.]?\d{3}[-.]?\d{4}\b',
                       '[PHONE]', text)                   # replace phone numbers
        return text

    def deduplicate(self, texts):
        """Remove exact duplicates."""
        seen = set()
        unique = []
        for text in texts:
            normalized = text.strip().lower()
            if normalized not in seen:
                seen.add(normalized)
                unique.append(text)
        removed = len(texts) - len(unique)
        self.stats['duplicates_removed'] = removed
        return unique


# ============================================================
# Part 3: Data Source Catalog
# ============================================================

DATA_SOURCES = {
    "Large-Scale Public Datasets": {
        "Common Crawl": {
            "size": "~250 TB (raw)",
            "description": "Monthly crawl of the web, billions of pages",
            "url": "commoncrawl.org",
            "license": "CC BY (metadata), content varies"
        },
        "The Pile": {
            "size": "~800 GB",
            "description": "22 curated sources: books, papers, code, web",
            "url": "pile.eleuther.ai",
            "license": "MIT (compilation), content varies"
        },
        "RedPajama": {
            "size": "~1.2 TB",
            "description": "Open reproduction of LLaMA training data",
            "url": "github.com/togethercomputer/RedPajama-Data",
            "license": "Apache 2.0"
        },
        "C4": {
            "size": "~750 GB",
            "description": "Cleaned Common Crawl, used for T5 training",
            "url": "huggingface.co/datasets/c4",
            "license": "ODC-BY"
        }
    },
    "Domain-Specific": {
        "arXiv": "2.3M+ scientific papers (bulk access available)",
        "Wikipedia": "All articles, 300+ languages, monthly dumps",
        "Project Gutenberg": "70,000+ public domain books",
        "The Stack": "6.4 TB of permissively licensed source code",
        "PubMed": "36M+ biomedical literature citations"
    }
}


# ============================================================
# DEMO
# ============================================================

print("=" * 60)
print("TRAINING DATA SOURCES & QUALITY PIPELINE")
print("=" * 60)

# Load simulated datasets
print("\n--- Loading Datasets ---")
wiki = load_dataset("wikitext")
shakespeare = load_dataset("tiny_shakespeare")
print(f"  WikiText: {wiki}")
print(f"  Shakespeare: {shakespeare}")

# Apply quality pipeline
print(f"\n--- Quality Pipeline ---")
pipeline = DataQualityPipeline(min_length=20)

all_texts = wiki.data + shakespeare.data
print(f"  Raw samples: {len(all_texts)}")

# Filter for quality
quality_texts = [t for t in all_texts if pipeline.is_quality(t)]
print(f"  After quality filter: {len(quality_texts)}")
print(f"  Filter stats: {dict(pipeline.stats)}")

# Clean
cleaned = [pipeline.clean(t) for t in quality_texts]
print(f"  After cleaning: {len(cleaned)}")

# Deduplicate
unique = pipeline.deduplicate(cleaned)
print(f"  After deduplication: {len(unique)}")
print(f"  Duplicates removed: {pipeline.stats['duplicates_removed']}")

# Show samples
print(f"\n--- Sample Processed Texts ---")
for i, text in enumerate(unique[:3]):
    preview = text[:100] + "..." if len(text) > 100 else text
    print(f"  [{i}] {preview}")

# Show data source catalog
print(f"\n--- Available Data Sources ---")
for category, sources in DATA_SOURCES.items():
    print(f"\n  {category}:")
    if isinstance(sources, dict):
        for name, info in sources.items():
            if isinstance(info, dict):
                print(f"    - {name}: {info['size']} | {info['description']}")
            else:
                print(f"    - {name}: {info}")

print(f"\n--- HuggingFace Usage (Production Code) ---")
print("""
  # Install: pip install datasets
  from datasets import load_dataset

  # Load a dataset
  dataset = load_dataset("wikitext", "wikitext-103-v1")
  train_data = dataset["train"]

  # Filter and preprocess
  filtered = train_data.filter(lambda x: len(x["text"]) > 50)
  print(f"Filtered: {len(filtered)} samples")

  # Stream large datasets (no download required)
  dataset = load_dataset("c4", "en", streaming=True)
  for sample in dataset["train"]:
      process(sample["text"])
      break  # just showing the pattern
""")

print("Done! Use these patterns to build your training corpus.")

"""
Unified LLM Provider Interface
===============================
Switch between your own model and commercial APIs with one config variable.
Demo mode: uses mock responses (no real API calls needed).

import time
import json

@dataclass
class LLMResponse:

    text: str
    provider: str
    model: str
    tokens_used: int
    latency_ms: float
    cost_estimate: float = 0.0
    metadata: dict = field(default_factory=dict)


class UnifiedLLMProvider:
    """
    Unified interface for multiple LLM backends.
    Switch providers with a single config variable.

    Supported providers:
    - "own"     : Your Mini GPT-2 model (local inference)

        self.default_provider = default_provider

        response += "The local model generates text quickly and privately. "

        # response = client.chat.completions.create(
        #     model="gpt-4",

        #     temperature=temperature,
        #     max_tokens=max_tokens
        # )
        # return response.choices[0].message.content, "gpt-4"

        time.sleep(0.3)  # Simulate API latency
        response = f"[OpenAI GPT-4] I'd be happy to help with: '{prompt[:50]}...'. "
        response += "This response demonstrates the OpenAI integration path. "
        response += "GPT-4 excels at complex reasoning and nuanced responses."
        return response, "gpt-4"

    def _generate_gemini(self, prompt, temperature, max_tokens):
        """Generate using Google Gemini API."""
        # In production:
        # import google.generativeai as genai
        # genai.configure(api_key=self.api_keys.get("gemini"))
        # model = genai.GenerativeModel("gemini-pro")
        # response = model.generate_content(
        #     prompt,
        #     generation_config={"temperature": temperature,
        #                        "max_output_tokens": max_tokens}
        # )
        # return response.text, "gemini-pro"

        time.sleep(0.25)
        response = f"[Gemini Pro] Analyzing your request: '{prompt[:50]}...'. "
        response += "This shows the Google Gemini integration. "
        response += "Gemini offers strong multilingual and multimodal capabilities."
        return response, "gemini-pro"

    def _generate_claude(self, prompt, temperature, max_tokens):
        """Generate using Anthropic Claude API."""
        # In production:
        # import anthropic
        # client = anthropic.Anthropic(api_key=self.api_keys.get("claude"))
        # response = client.messages.create(
        #     model="claude-sonnet-4-20250514",
        #     max_tokens=max_tokens,
        #     messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}]
        # )
        # return response.content[0].text, "claude-sonnet-4-20250514"

        time.sleep(0.2)
        response = f"[Claude] I'll help with: '{prompt[:50]}...'. "
        response += "This demonstrates the Anthropic Claude integration. "
        response += "Claude is known for careful, nuanced, and safe responses."
        return response, "claude-sonnet-4-20250514"

    # ---- Main interface ----

    def generate(self, prompt, temperature=0.7, max_tokens=256,
                 provider=None):
        """
        Generate text using the specified (or default) provider.
        This is the ONE method you call - provider switching is config-driven.
        """
        provider = provider or self.default_provider

        generators = {
            "own": self._generate_own,
            "openai": self._generate_openai,
            "gemini": self._generate_gemini,
            "claude": self._generate_claude,
        }

        if provider not in generators:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown provider: {provider}. "
                           f"Choose from: {list(generators.keys())}")

        start = time.time()
        text, model = generators[provider](prompt, temperature, max_tokens)
        latency = (time.time() - start) * 1000

        tokens = len(text.split())
        pricing = self.PRICING[provider]
        cost = (tokens / 1000) * pricing["output"]

        self._call_count[provider] += 1

        return LLMResponse(
            text=text,
            provider=provider,
            model=model,
            tokens_used=tokens,
            latency_ms=round(latency, 1),
            cost_estimate=round(cost, 6),
            metadata={"temperature": temperature, "max_tokens": max_tokens}
        )

    def get_stats(self):
        """Return usage statistics."""
        return {
            "default_provider": self.default_provider,
            "calls_by_provider": dict(self._call_count),
            "total_calls": sum(self._call_count.values())
        }


# ============================================================
# DEMO
# ============================================================

print("=" * 60)
print("UNIFIED LLM PROVIDER - DEMO")
print("=" * 60)

# Initialize with your own model as default
llm = UnifiedLLMProvider(
    default_provider="own",
    api_keys={
        "openai": "sk-xxx",
        "gemini": "AIza-xxx",
        "claude": "sk-ant-xxx",
    }
)

prompt = "Explain how transformers use self-attention"

# Test each provider
print("\n--- Testing All Providers ---\n")

for provider in ["own", "openai", "gemini", "claude"]:
    response = llm.generate(prompt, provider=provider)
    print(f"Provider: {response.provider} ({response.model})")
    print(f"  Response: {response.text[:80]}...")
    print(f"  Latency: {response.latency_ms}ms | "
          f"Tokens: {response.tokens_used} | "
          f"Cost: ${response.cost_estimate:.6f}")
    print()

# Show config-driven switching
print("--- Config-Driven Switching ---\n")
print("Change one variable to switch providers:\n")

for provider_name in ["own", "claude", "openai"]:
    llm.default_provider = provider_name
    r = llm.generate("What is machine learning?")
    print(f"  default_provider = '{provider_name}' -> "
          f"Used {r.provider} ({r.model}), "
          f"latency={r.latency_ms}ms, cost=${r.cost_estimate:.6f}")

# Usage stats
print(f"\n--- Usage Statistics ---")
stats = llm.get_stats()
print(f"  Total calls: {stats['total_calls']}")
for provider, count in stats['calls_by_provider'].items():
    if count > 0:
        print(f"  {provider}: {count} calls")

print(f"\n--- Hybrid Strategy Example ---")
print("""
  # In production, use your own model for simple/private tasks
  # and fall back to commercial APIs for complex tasks:

  def smart_generate(prompt, complexity="low"):
      if complexity == "low" or is_sensitive(prompt):
          return llm.generate(prompt, provider="own")   # Fast, free, private
      elif complexity == "high":
          return llm.generate(prompt, provider="claude") # Best quality
      else:
          return llm.generate(prompt, provider="gemini") # Good balance
""")

print("Done! Your unified LLM provider is ready.")

# docker-compose.yml
# Full-stack LLM Application
# Run: docker compose up --build

version: "3.9"

services:
  # --- Frontend (Nginx serving static files) ---
  frontend:
    image: nginx:alpine
    ports:
      - "3000:80"
    volumes:
      - ./frontend:/usr/share/nginx/html:ro
      - ./nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:ro
    depends_on:
      api:
        condition: service_healthy
    restart: unless-stopped

  # --- API Server (FastAPI + Uvicorn) ---
  api:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: Dockerfile.api
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
    environment:
      - API_KEY=${API_KEY:-dev-key-change-me}
      - MODEL_PATH=/app/models/mini_gpt2.npz
      - DEFAULT_PROVIDER=${DEFAULT_PROVIDER:-own}
      - OPENAI_API_KEY=${OPENAI_API_KEY:-}
      - GOOGLE_API_KEY=${GOOGLE_API_KEY:-}
      - ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY:-}
      - MAX_TOKENS=${MAX_TOKENS:-256}
      - CORS_ORIGINS=http://localhost:3000
    volumes:
      - model-weights:/app/models
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost:8000/health"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 2G

volumes:
  model-weights:
    driver: local

#!/bin/bash
# deploy.sh - Quick Deploy to Railway or Render
# Usage: ./deploy.sh [railway|render]
# Prerequisites: Git repository initialized, Railway CLI or Render account

set -euo pipefail

PLATFORM="${1:-railway}"

echo "============================================"
echo "  LLM Stack Deployment - ${PLATFORM}"
echo "============================================"

# Step 1: Pre-flight checks
echo ""
echo "[Step 1] Pre-flight checks..."

# Check Git status
if ! git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "ERROR: Not in a git repository. Run 'git init' first."
    exit 1
fi

# Check for uncommitted changes
if ! git diff-index --quiet HEAD --; then
    echo "WARNING: You have uncommitted changes."
    echo "  Run 'git add . && git commit -m "deploy"' first."
    read -p "  Continue anyway? (y/N) " -n 1 -r
    echo
    [[ $REPLY =~ ^[Yy]$ ]] || exit 1
fi

# Step 2: Verify required files exist
echo "[Step 2] Verifying project structure..."

required_files=("main.py" "requirements.txt" "frontend/index.html")
for file in "${required_files[@]}"; do
    if [ -f "$file" ]; then
        echo "  ✓ $file"
    else
        echo "  ✗ $file (MISSING)"
        echo "  Create this file before deploying."
    fi
done

# Step 3: Create deployment config if needed
echo "[Step 3] Setting up deployment config..."

if [ "$PLATFORM" = "railway" ]; then
    # --- Railway Deployment ---
    echo "  Platform: Railway (railway.app)"

    # Check for Railway CLI
    if ! command -v railway &> /dev/null; then
        echo "  Installing Railway CLI..."
        echo "  Run: npm install -g @railway/cli"
        echo "  Then: railway login"
        exit 1
    fi

    # Create Procfile if not exists
    if [ ! -f "Procfile" ]; then
        echo "web: uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port \$PORT" > Procfile
        echo "  Created Procfile"
    fi

    # Deploy
    echo ""
    echo "[Step 4] Deploying to Railway..."
    echo "  railway up"
    echo ""
    echo "  After deployment, set environment variables:"
    echo "    railway variables set API_KEY=your-secure-key"
    echo "    railway variables set DEFAULT_PROVIDER=own"
    echo "    railway variables set MODEL_PATH=/app/models/mini_gpt2.npz"

elif [ "$PLATFORM" = "render" ]; then
    # --- Render Deployment ---
    echo "  Platform: Render (render.com)"

    # Create render.yaml if not exists
    if [ ! -f "render.yaml" ]; then
        cat > render.yaml << 'YAML'
services:
  - type: web
    name: llm-api
    runtime: python
    buildCommand: pip install -r requirements.txt
    startCommand: uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT
    envVars:
      - key: API_KEY
        generateValue: true
      - key: DEFAULT_PROVIDER
        value: own
      - key: MODEL_PATH
        value: /app/models/mini_gpt2.npz
      - key: PYTHON_VERSION
        value: "3.11"
    healthCheckPath: /health
  - type: web
    name: llm-frontend
    runtime: static
    buildCommand: echo "Static site"
    staticPublishPath: ./frontend
    headers:
      - path: /*
        name: Cache-Control
        value: public, max-age=3600
    routes:
      - type: rewrite
        source: /api/*
        destination: https://llm-api.onrender.com/*
YAML
        echo "  Created render.yaml"
    fi

    echo ""
    echo "[Step 4] To deploy to Render:"
    echo "  1. Push your code to GitHub"
    echo "  2. Go to dashboard.render.com"
    echo "  3. Click 'New' -> 'Blueprint'"
    echo "  4. Connect your GitHub repo"
    echo "  5. Render will auto-detect render.yaml"
fi

# Step 5: Post-deployment checklist
echo ""
echo "============================================"
echo "  POST-DEPLOYMENT CHECKLIST"
echo "============================================"
echo ""
echo "  [ ] Set API_KEY environment variable"
echo "  [ ] Upload model weights to /app/models/"
echo "  [ ] Test health endpoint: curl https://your-url/health"
echo "  [ ] Test generate endpoint with API key"
echo "  [ ] Update frontend API_URL to production URL"
echo "  [ ] Enable HTTPS (usually automatic)"
echo "  [ ] Set up monitoring/alerting"
echo "  [ ] Configure rate limiting"
echo ""
echo "Done! Your LLM stack is ready for deployment."
